subtopic: Geometry of Complex Numbers (Argand Geometry & Loci)
title: The rotation theorem

board_content.text: Rotation = multiply the displacement by e^{i theta}
To rotate $\vec{AB}$ about $A$ by angle $\theta$, multiply $z_B-z_A$ by $e^{i\theta}$.

board_content.caption: Angle at the common vertex, between two displacements

board_content.text: The angle is measured at the common vertex $z_1$, from $\vec{z_1z_3}$ to $\vec{z_1z_2}$.
Reversing the ratio reverses the angle's sign.
This single move finds a third vertex, proves a right angle, or builds a square.

segments_english.text: The rotation theorem is the single most powerful tool in Argand geometry. It solves a huge class of configuration problems in one line.
The core idea: to rotate the vector from A to B about the point A through an angle theta, you multiply the displacement z B minus z A by e to the i theta.
Picture three points forming a triangle, with two displacement vectors leaving the common vertex z one, and an angle theta between them.
The theorem packages that as a ratio: z two minus z one, over z three minus z one, equals the ratio of their lengths times e to the i theta, where theta is the argument of that same ratio.
Read the geometry carefully: the angle sits at the common vertex z one, measured from the direction of z one to z three, turning toward z one to z two.
And mind the order: reversing the ratio, swapping which displacement is on top, reverses the sign of the angle. Getting this backwards is the rotation-sign error.
With this one move you can find an unknown third vertex, prove that an angle is a right angle, or construct a square or an equilateral triangle.
Keep the direction convention firm: multiplying by e to the i theta rotates anticlockwise, while e to the minus i theta rotates clockwise.

segments_hinglish.text: Rotation theorem Argand geometry ka sabse powerful tool hai. Ye configuration problems ki ek badi class ek line mein solve karta hai.
Core idea: A se B tak ke vector ko point A ke baare mein angle theta se rotate karne ke liye, aap displacement z B minus z A ko e to the i theta se multiply karo.
Teen points ko triangle banate socho, do displacement vectors common vertex z one se nikalte hue, aur unke beech ek angle theta.
Theorem ise ek ratio ki tarah package karta hai: z two minus z one, over z three minus z one, barabar unki lengths ka ratio times e to the i theta, jahan theta hai usi ratio ka argument.
Geometry dhyaan se padho: angle common vertex z one par baithta hai, z one se z three ki direction se naapa, z one se z two ki taraf ghoomte hue.
Aur order dhyaan se: ratio ulta karna, upar kaun sa displacement hai wo swap karna, angle ka sign ulta kar deta hai. Ise ulta karna rotation-sign error hai.
Is ek move se aap ek unknown teesra vertex nikaal sakte ho, prove kar sakte ho ki koi angle right angle hai, ya ek square ya equilateral triangle bana sakte ho.
Direction convention pakka rakho: e to the i theta se multiply karna anticlockwise rotate karta hai, jabki e to the minus i theta clockwise.
